name: Kruger National Park
description: Africa's greatest game reserve — Big Five, 500+ bird species, and 2 million hectares of wilderness.
feeDetail: Standard conservation fee ~R486/day for international adults (2025/26 SANParks tariff). Wild Card available.

name: Table Mountain National Park
description: Iconic flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town — fynbos, penguins at Boulders Beach, and dramatic coastal trails.
feeDetail: Table Mountain Cableway from ~R420 return (2025). Park entry at Boulders penguin beach separate.

name: Addo Elephant National Park
description: Home to over 600 elephants and the only park offering Big Seven (including great white sharks and southern right whales).
feeDetail: Conservation fee ~R376/day international adults. Marine eco-tours extra.

name: Etosha National Park
description: One of Africa's oldest parks — centred on a vast salt pan, with legendary floodlit waterhole viewing.
feeDetail: NWR park fee ~N$142/person/day + N$30/vehicle (2025 rates).

name: Namib-Naukluft Park
description: One of the world's largest conservation areas — Sossusvlei's red dunes and the oldest desert on Earth.
feeDetail: Sesriem/Sossusvlei access ~N$142/person + vehicle fee. Sossusvlei gate opens before sunrise for dune visits.

name: Skeleton Coast Park
description: Where desert meets the Atlantic — shipwrecks, fur seal colonies, and desert-adapted lions.
feeDetail: Restricted access — permit via NWR/Dorob-Skeleton Coast. Tour operators arrange access.

name: Chobe National Park
description: Africa's largest elephant population — 120,000 elephants and spectacular Chobe River cruises.
feeDetail: Park fee ~P120/person/day + P$10 vehicle (approx. 2025). River cruise fees separate.

name: Moremi Game Reserve
description: The Okavango Delta's wildlife heartland — mokoro trips, leopard sightings, and pristine floodplains.
feeDetail: Moremi Game Reserve fee ~P120/person/day. Mokoro trips booked via lodges.

name: Central Kalahari Game Reserve
description: Vast semi-arid wilderness — black-maned lions, brown hyenas, and the raw Kalahari experience.
feeDetail: Lower park fees but remote — fuel and self-sufficiency essential.

name: South Luangwa National Park
description: Birthplace of the walking safari — legendary leopard sightings and hippo-filled Luangwa River.
feeDetail: Park fee ~$30/day international visitors. Walking safaris require licensed guide.

name: Kafue National Park
description: One of Africa's largest parks — Busanga Plains cheetah, tree-climbing lions, and remote wilderness.
feeDetail: Park entry ~$20/day. Busanga Plains seasonal (dry season only).

name: Lower Zambezi National Park
description: Canoe safaris along the Zambezi — elephants, hippos, and stunning escarpment views.
feeDetail: Park fee ~$20/day. Canoe safaris arranged via lodges.

name: Hwange National Park
description: Zimbabwe's largest reserve — 100+ mammal species across ancient elephant migration corridors.
feeDetail: Park fee ~$15/day. Main camp waterholes best at dry season dusk.

name: Mana Pools National Park
description: UNESCO World Heritage wilderness — walking safaris among elephants and albida trees on the Zambezi floodplain.
feeDetail: UNESCO wilderness — walking permits required. Book camps in advance.

name: Gonarezhou National Park
description: Remote wilderness in the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park — Chilojo Cliffs and untamed bush.
feeDetail: Remote 4x4 park. Chilojo Cliffs viewpoint highlight.

name: Gorongosa National Park
description: Africa's greatest wildlife restoration story — lions, elephants, and thriving ecosystems reborn.
feeDetail: Park fee ~$20/day. Restoration success story — guided drives recommended.

name: Bazaruto Archipelago National Park
description: Turquoise Indian Ocean islands — dugongs, whale sharks, and world-class diving.
feeDetail: Marine park fees vary by activity. Dhow and dive permits through operators.

name: Quirimbas National Park
description: Remote northern archipelago — mangroves, coral reefs, and Swahili-influenced island culture.
feeDetail: Remote northern archipelago — fly-in lodges include park access.

name: Liwonde National Park
description: Malawi's premier wildlife reserve — boat safaris on the Shire River alongside elephants and crocs.
feeDetail: Park fee ~$25/day. Boat safaris on Shire River extra.

name: Nyika National Park
description: High-altitude plateau of rolling grasslands — zebras, antelope, and wild orchids.
feeDetail: Plateau park ~$20/day. Cool climate — pack layers.

name: Lake Malawi National Park
description: UNESCO site on the lake shore — 1,000+ cichlid species and crystal-clear snorkelling.
feeDetail: Lake shore park ~$10/day. Snorkelling fees at Cape Maclear.

name: Sehlabathebe National Park
description: Remote highland wilderness — rock art, wild horses, and dramatic Drakensberg escarpment scenery.
feeDetail: Remote highland park — 4x4 recommended.

name: Tse'ehlanyane National Park
description: Maloti Mountains sanctuary — indigenous forests, trout fishing, and alpine hiking trails.
feeDetail: Maloti Mountains entry ~M50/day.

name: Bokong Nature Reserve
description: Stunning plateau above the Katse Dam — bearded vultures, alpine flowers, and panoramic views.
feeDetail: Katse Dam plateau reserve ~M50/day.

name: Hlane Royal National Park
description: Eswatini's largest park — lions, rhinos, and guided game drives in royal bushveld.
feeDetail: Big Game Parks fee ~E250/day. Guided drives for lion enclosure.

name: Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Eswatini's pioneer conservation area — walk or cycle among antelope, hippos, and crocodiles.
feeDetail: Sanctuary entry ~E80/day. Walking and cycling included.

name: Malolotja Nature Reserve
description: Pristine montane wilderness — canopy tours, hiking trails, and the Malolotja Falls.
feeDetail: Nature reserve ~E50/day. Canopy tour separate booking.
